A Pictorial Guide to Installing Kali Linux on your Android Device

Nureni Jamiu O. on 2022-11-22

Installing Kali Linux on an Android Device is a simple process that could be completed in less than 30mins when done correctly.

Kali is a powerful distribution of Linux made by hackers specifically for hackers. It is vastly used for, but not limited to Penetration Testing. It has a wider usability coverage which extends from basic Penetration Testing to advanced Penetration Testing, Security Research, Computer Forensics, Malware Analysis, Reverse Engineering… not to mention but a few.

While Kali Linux seems to be most popular on Laptops and Desktop devices, its versatility also extends to functioning on a variety of mobile devices. In this article, I’ll be walking you through every step of how to have Kali running on your Android device in no time. That said, let’s dive right in!

Requirements:

  • An Android device running on a minimum version 7.0 or newer. This installation will likely succeed on Android devices running on version 12, but it is not recommend due to some fatalities recorded as a result of a high CPU usage. To learn more about this issue, here’s a github link to where the issue is addressed: https://github.com/termux/termux-app/issues/2366
  • You’ll also need Termux which can be downloaded from f-droid website or directly from their Github repository using either of the links below(We’ll be downloading from the website in this Demo).

https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/

https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases

Note: It is important to know that downloading from Google Playstore is downloading an outdated version, and a numerous update could be missing.

Installation Guide

  1. Visit the first link provided above to download Termux. Scroll down and Click on “Download APK” then accept any warning prompt about the APK being harmful. Your file should start downloading immmediately. You can check your ‘downloads’ tab to confirm.

2. Once downloaded, click on it to install the application. Follow the screen instructions and after installation, open the app and start by typing the following commands which basically updates and upgrades your packages.

$ apt update $$ apt upgrade

Press “y” if any prompt appears asking you to confirm if you do want to continue the upgrade.

3. Next is to check the architecture of your phone by typing the following command…

$ getprop ro.product.cpu.abi

The output would show you if you’re running on a 64bit or 32bit architecture. For this walkthrough, I’m running on a 64bit architecture as seen in the image below.

You’ll get a “arm64-v8a” output if you’re running on a 64bit architecture and a “armeabi” or “armeabi-v7a” output if you’re running on a 32bit architecture.

4. Next is to open your browser(This is the last time you’ll be interacting with your browser during this installation process) and navigate to this link below if you’re running on a 64bit architecture…

http://kali.download/nethunter-images/current/rootfs/kalifs-arm64-full.tar.xz

…or this link below if you’re running on a 32bit…

http://kali.download/nethunter-images/current/rootfs/kalifs-armhf-full.tar.xz

Once pasted into your browser, the kali-arm file will begin downloading immediately. You can always confirm that by checking your browser’s downloads tab.

5. Once downloaded, back in Termux, you need to give Termux access to your phone’s internal storage. This can be done by typing the following command and then press “y” if prompted for a ‘continue’ confirmation.

$ termux-setup-storage

6. Next is to type the following commands…

$ cd storage

$ ls

$ cd downloads

…which basically switches you into your internal storage’s download directory.

6. Listing the contents of the downloads directory using the “ls” command, you can see that the downloaded kali-arm image load file is present in the directory.

7. The next step is to move this file back into the user’s home directory using the following command.

$ mv kalifs-arm64-full.tar.xz /$HOME

8. Now switch back into the home directory by typing “cd”, then type in the following commands.

$ apt install wget

$ wget -O install-nethunter-termux https://offs.ec/2MceZWr

…which installs “wget” and downloads the Nethunter installer script respectively.

9. The next thing is to make the script executable by changing the file’s permission using this following command.

$ chmod +x install-nethunter-termux

and then finally executing the script.

$ ./install-nethunter-termux

This will then automate the installation process. For any prompt that may show up afterward, your response should be a “n”. Then leave it while it does its thing… This may take a while… so while at it, you may want to grab a cup of coffee real quick… ☕

Once the installation is done, you’ll be greeted with the Kali screen with some basic guide on how to navigate the new environment.

A big congratulations to you if you made it this far! 🎉

…however, it isn’t over yet. This is just the CLI. We want the full installation which equally covers the GUI. In order to achieve this, we’ll have to open our browser once again. Oh! I know it! I know I said earlier that that would be the last time you opened your browser… ‘Forgive me for I didn’t know what I was saying’.😁 This time, for real, will be the last time, so let’s move on...👇👇👇

10. Copy and paste this link into your browser to download the Nethunter Store Application and complete the installation process.

https://store.nethunter.com/en/

11. Once installed, open it and in the search bar, type “Nethunter Kex”.

12. Download the app and complete the installation process. After a successful installation, you should have an icon similar to the one in the image below.

13. In your terminal, type “nh kex” or “nethunter kex”

$ nethunter kex

Since this is the first time, you’ll be prompted to set a password. Type in your password, verify it and most importantly, make sure you remember it, for it will be needed in one of the concluding steps.

Also, make sure to save the port number somewhere because you’ll need this later too. In our case, the port that kex is running on is “5901".

14. Now open the “Nethunter Kex” application downloaded in step 12 above. Set the first input field to be “NetHunter KeX”, the second field as “localhost”, the little field by the right should occupy your port number generated in step 13 which in my case is “5901", the next field below as “kali”, the last field as your Kex password which was also set in step 13, and lastly, mark the “keep” checkbox to keep your settings for later usage. Every step mentioned can be seen in the image below.

15. …and lastly, here comes the MAGIC we’ve been waiting for! Click the “connect” button at the top-right corner and…(/*sips some coffee*/) Boom! Magic!! And just like that… we’re in!. Like…We did it! YOU did it!!!💪💥✌

Welcome to the Kali World! The abode of great Hackers. Get ready to dine with the Big Boys😊… and remember that with great power comes great responsibility.
